classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1936.htm (Статьи 33-36: two chambers, one Soviet of the Union deputy per 300,000 inhabitants, Soviet of Nationalities seats per republic, oblast, and okrug, four-year term; статьи 134-142: direct, secret ballot in districts)
classes.note: Each elector voted in two single-member districts, one for each chamber; the candidates stood for the bloc of communists and non-party people, and a voter could vote against by crossing out the name, so the reports give votes for and against each chamber's candidates. The Central Electoral Commission for each election reported the electorate, turnout, and votes for and against by chamber and union republic. Under the 1977 Constitution the term became five years and each chamber had 750 deputies. The Supreme Soviet chosen in 1989 was elected by the Congress of People's Deputies (class verkhovny_sovet_1989).

classes.name_en: Congress of Soviets of the USSR and its Central Executive Committee
classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1924.htm (Глава третья, 9-10: delegates of city soviets and provincial congresses of soviets, elected at the provincial or republican congresses; 14: the Congress elects the Union Soviet of the Central Executive Committee)
classes.disposition_reason: From 1922 to 1936 the supreme organ was the Congress of Soviets of the USSR, whose delegates were chosen by the city soviets and by the provincial or republican congresses of soviets, not by the voters; the Congress in turn elected the Central Executive Committee. No public vote chose an all-Union body before the Supreme Soviet election of 12 December 1937.

classes.note: The Congress of People's Deputies had 2,250 deputies: 750 from territorial districts, 750 from national-territorial districts in the union and autonomous republics, autonomous oblasts, and autonomous okrugs, and 750 from public organizations (class obshchestvennye_organizatsii). In the districts one, two, or more candidates stood; where more than two stood and none was elected, the two leaders went to repeat voting (art. 60 of the Law on elections of people's deputies of the USSR), and where one or two stood and none was elected, or turnout was under half, a repeat election with new nominations followed (art. 61). Elections to replace deputies who left were also held in single districts.

cadence.runoff_rule: Repeat voting between the two leading candidates where more than two stood and none was elected (art. 60); a repeat election with new nominations where one or two stood and none was elected, or under half the electors voted (art. 61)

access.evidence: The Central Electoral Commission's reports on the 26 March 1989 election, the repeat voting of 2 and 9 April, and the repeat elections of 14 May, with totals by kind of district and turnout by union republic; district results went to local papers

dates.quote: было образовано 750 территориальных избирательных округов ... было образовано 750 национально-территориальных избирательных округов
dates.note: Held in 749 territorial and 748 national-territorial districts; 1,226 deputies elected in the districts. 172,840,130 of 192,575,165 electors voted. The 750 deputies of public organizations are in obshchestvennye_organizatsii.

dates.quote: 2 и 9 апреля 1989 года состоялось повторное голосование в 46 территориальных и 30 национально-территориальных избирательных округах
dates.note: First of the two days of repeat voting between the two leading candidates in districts with more than two candidates where no one was elected; over both days 76 districts (46 territorial, 30 national-territorial) voted and 76 deputies were elected. The report does not split the districts by day.

dates.quote: 2 и 9 апреля 1989 года состоялось повторное голосование в 46 территориальных и 30 национально-территориальных избирательных округах
dates.note: Second of the two days of repeat voting; see 2 April 1989 for the 76 districts held over both days.

dates.quote: повторные выборы, проведенные 14 мая по 198 избирательным округам
dates.note: Repeat elections with new nominations in 114 territorial and 84 national-territorial districts; 71 deputies elected and 126 districts sent to repeat voting, whose date the report does not give.

classes.name: Выборы народных депутатов СССР от общественных организаций
classes.name_en: Congress of People's Deputies: deputies of public organizations
classes.locator: https://dspace.nplg.gov.ge/handle/1234/538952 (Выборы по территориальным округам; Выборы по национально-территориальным избирательным округам; Итоги выборов от общественных организаций)
classes.disposition_reason: 750 of the 2,250 people's deputies were elected by the congresses, conferences, or plenums of the all-Union bodies of public organizations (871 candidates for the 750 seats in March 1989; repeat elections in April and May 1989 in, among others, the Academy of Sciences, the Union of Artists, and the Soviet Peace Fund), not by the voters.

classes.name: Избрание Верховного Совета СССР Съездом народных депутатов
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet of the USSR elected by the Congress of People's Deputies, 1989-1991
classes.locator: https://dspace.nplg.gov.ge/handle/1234/539549 (26 May 1989: the Congress proceeds to the election of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR, by secret ballot on agreed lists of deputies)
classes.disposition_reason: From 1989 the two chambers of the Supreme Soviet were elected by the Congress of People's Deputies from among its members, first by secret ballot on 26 May 1989; no public vote chose them.

classes.name: Выборы Президента СССР
classes.locator: https://dspace.nplg.gov.ge/handle/1234/540636 (Закон СССР об учреждении поста Президента СССР: art. 127-1, popular election for five years; part III, the first President elected by the Congress of People's Deputies; the Congress's resolution electing M. S. Gorbachev)
classes.disposition_reason: The 1990 law provided for a President elected by the citizens for five years, but made the first President an election by the Congress of People's Deputies; the Congress elected M. S. Gorbachev in March 1990, he resigned on 25 December 1991, and the office ended without any popular presidential election.

classes.name: Референдум СССР
classes.finest_note: Totals for the Union and for each republic that voted, in the Central Commission of the Referendum's report and the Supreme Soviet's resolution of 21 March 1991.
classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1977.htm (Статья 5: the most important questions are put to a nationwide vote, a referendum)
classes.note: The 1977 Constitution allowed referendums, and the Law of 21 December 1990 on the nationwide vote (referendum of the USSR) set the procedure; the only referendum, on preserving the Union as a renewed federation, was held on 17 March 1991 in nine republics. Armenia, Georgia, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldavia, and Estonia did not hold it.

access.platform: Президентская библиотека имени Б. Н. Ельцина
access.evidence: National electorate, turnout, and yes vote, citing the Supreme Soviet's resolution on the results

dates.quote: Из 185,6 млн. граждан СССР, включённых в списки для голосования, в референдуме приняли участие 148,5 млн. (79,5%); из них 113,5 млн. (76,43%) высказались за сохранение СССР.
dates.note: Held in 9 of the 15 union republics. Questions a republic put to its own voters on the same day belong to that republic's census.

classes.name: Выборы в Верховные Советы союзных республик
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviets of the union republics
classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1936.htm (Статьи 57-59: the Supreme Soviet of a union republic, elected by its citizens, with representation set by the republic's constitution)
classes.disposition_reason: Each union republic elected its own Supreme Soviet under its own constitution and electoral law, from 1938 to the competitive elections of 1990; these elections are counted in the census of each successor state (for example the classes soviet_rsfsr and congress_rsfsr of Russia, supreme_soviet_ssr of Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, and Uzbekistan), not again here.

classes.name: Выборы в местные Советы
classes.locator: https://dspace.nplg.gov.ge/handle/1234/468322 (leading article: the elections to the local soviets of working people's deputies, held the day before, 24 December 1939); the 1936 Constitution, arts. 94-96, set two-year terms
classes.disposition_reason: Local soviets were elected under the union republics' constitutions and regulations, first on 24 December 1939, every two years and from 1977 every two and a half years; these elections are counted in each successor state's census (for example soviets_local of Russia and local_soviets_ssr of Ukraine), not again here.

classes.name: Выборы народных судей
classes.name_en: People's judges of the district and city courts
classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1977.htm (Статья 152: people's judges of district and city courts elected by the citizens for five years; people's assessors elected at meetings by open vote)
classes.disposition_reason: People's judges of the district and city courts were elected by the citizens under the 1936 and 1977 Constitutions, but in elections the union republics organized and reported; they belong to the successor states' censuses. People's assessors were chosen by open vote at meetings of workers and residents, and the higher courts by the soviets.

classes.name: Отзыв депутата Верховного Совета СССР
classes.name_en: Recall of a deputy of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR
classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1936.htm (Статья 142: every deputy reports to the voters and may be recalled at any time by decision of a majority of the voters)
classes.note: The 1936 and 1977 Constitutions let a majority of a district's voters recall their deputy. The sources read here list no recall vote of a deputy of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR, so the class has no dates yet.

classes.name: Выдвижение кандидатов
classes.name_en: Nomination of candidates and party bodies
classes.locator: http://www.hist.msu.ru/ER/Etext/cnst1977.htm (Статья 100: candidates nominated by the organizations of the CPSU, the trade unions, the Komsomol, cooperatives, other public organizations, labor collectives, and meetings of servicemen)
classes.disposition_reason: Candidates were nominated by party, trade-union, and Komsomol organizations, labor collectives, and meetings of servicemen; the CPSU chose its bodies at its own congresses. The state ran and published no primaries.
